newsitem.title: USA: UPS deal gives Clinton a birthday gift.
newsitem.headline: UPS deal gives Clinton a birthday gift.

text.p: When it comes to enjoying carefree holidays, Bill Clinton is the luckiest president in a long time -- as the tentative settlement of the United Parcel Service strike illustrates.

With its potential for harming the booming U.S. economy, the labor row between UPS and its unionized workers was Clinton's only major worry as he plunged into a three-week vacation on Martha's Vineyard, an island playground for the rich and famous 12 miles off the Massachusetts coast.

The settlement was a real political and personal lift for Clinton, who celebrated his 51st birthday Tuesday by going jogging in public for the first time since he tore a tendon in his right knee last March.
He was so elated by the deal, which came after he and Labor Secretary Alexis Herman prodded the parties to resolve their differences, that he met with reporters to do some crowing.

"I would like to compliment UPS and the Teamsters on resolving their differences," Clinton said. "I think it is very much in the interest not only of the company and its employees but also of all the people it serves and of the United States, and I'm very pleased about it."

Clinton said he and his family would observe his birthday by "reading and playing games and having fun with each other" at a seaside hideaway loaned them by Boston businessman Richard Friedman. Hollywood couple Ted Danson and Mary Steenburgen were throwing a birthday party for him later.

"I feel very blessed," Clinton said. "As far as I know, I'm in good health and the country is doing well -- that's the most important thing of all. So I'm very happy today and I have a lot to be thankful for."

Once again, vacation magic seemed to be working for Clinton, who is riding high in the polls in the fifth year of a presidency full of ups and downs. Only once since he entered the White House has his August holiday been marred by trouble - - in 1995, when three U.S. diplomats were killed in Bosnia when their armored vehicle slid down a hillside.
Clinton, who was relaxing in Jackson Hole, Wyo. when the accident occurred, returned to Washington for a memorial service and flew back to resume his vacation the same day.

Other recent presidents have not been so lucky in getting away from it all. Ronald Reagan, who served in the White House from 1981 to 1989, had to cope with crises in the Middle East during several of his vacations -- and in 1983, had to cut short a California holiday because of the Soviet downing of a Korean Airlines jumbo jet.

George Bush seemed even more snakebit when he tried to escape the cares and duties of office. Iraq triggered a crisis that led to the Gulf War by invading Kuwait days before he started his annual Maine vacation in 1990, and communist hardliners nearly ousted then-Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev from power while Bush was taking time off in 1991.
"What is it about August?" Bush groaned after the Moscow coup attempt.
Thanks to the settlement of the UPS strike, Clinton's vacation seems likely to be headache-free. While flying to Martha's Vineyard, he told a reporter he was looking forward to a rest.
